title: Further Safeguards Following Investigation into Recent Detention of 16-year-old Self-radicalised Singaporean
what_it_is: Further Safeguards Following Investigation into Recent Detention of 16-year-old Self-radicalised Singaporean

sections.label: Legal tools against self-radicalised terror suspects
sections.summary: Questions ask what further legal tools, measures and legislation changes can help detect, denounce and prevent self-radicalised terror attacks in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the recent detention of a 16-year-old Singaporean who planned and prepared to conduct terrorist attacks against Muslims in Singapore, what further legal tools should be put in place to bolster and support the Home Team’s operational capability to detect, trace and apprehend self-radicalised terror suspects before any terror incident occurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs what further measures can be undertaken to denounce terror attacks, whenever they take place around the globe, so as to prevent self-radicalised copy-cats from thinking they can replicate such horrific terror attacks in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs what legal measures can be undertaken to tighten up the Arms and Explosives Act (Chapter 13), or other relevant legislation, so as to prevent self-radicalised members of the public from getting their hands on firearms or explosives to carry out terror attacks in Singapore.

sections.label: 16-year-old arrested for mosque attack plans
sections.summary: A 16-year-old Singaporean was arrested in December 2020 after planning machete attacks on Muslims at two mosques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The 16-year-old Singaporean was arrested in December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: He had made detailed plans and preparations to attack Muslims at two mosques using a machete.

sections.label: ISIS videos and planned mosque attacks
sections.summary: He watched ISIS propaganda, wrongly concluded ISIS represented Islam, and planned attacks on 15 March 2021 at Assyafaah and Yusof Ishak Mosques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: He also watched propaganda videos produced by the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria, or ISIS, and came to the erroneous conclusion that ISIS represented Islam, and that Islam called on its followers to kill non-Muslims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: He had planned to carry out attacks on 15 March 2021, the second anniversary of the Christchurch attacks, at Assyafaah Mosque and Yusof Ishak Mosque, near his home.

sections.label: School Counsellors attended workshops
sections.summary: As of 2019, over 260 Secondary school School Counsellors and some Student Welfare Officers attended the workshops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: As of 2019, over 260 School Counsellors in Secondary schools, as well as a number of Student Welfare Officers, have attended the workshops.

sections.label: RRG digital outreach since COVID-19
sections.summary: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, the RRG intensified digital outreach, producing over 60 online lectures, postings, engagements and videos for the community, including youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, the RRG has intensified its digital outreach efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: It produced over 60 online lectures, "live" postings, online engagements and videos for the community, including for youths.

sections.label: Social cohesion sessions and hackathon
sections.summary: Since 2019, five sessions drew over 500 participants, and MCCY held a 2020 Hackathon for Social Cohesion with over 200 youths pitching ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Since 2019, five sessions have been organised, involving a total of more than 500 participants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: MCCY organised a Hackathon for Social Cohesion in November and December 2020, where more than 200 youths were invited to pitch innovative ideas on strengthening social cohesion and implement projects that promote social, racial and religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: We will continue to strengthen our efforts to build a resilient community that is prepared for a terrorist attack in Singapore and plays an active part to safeguard Singapore's unity in the face of this threat.

sections.label: ISD rehabilitation approach
sections.summary: ISD's rehabilitation approach is holistic, intensive and long-term, comprising religious, psychological and social rehabilitation together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The rehabilitation approach adopted by ISD is a holistic, intensive and long-term one, comprising religious, psychological and social rehabilitation – these three factors together.

sections.label: Addressing non-ideological radicalisation factors
sections.summary: Additional attention addresses non-ideological factors behind the youth's radicalisation, including belonging, critical thinking, resilience and stresses, and enabling education where practicable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Additional attention is also paid and in this case, to this 16-year-old youth, to address the non-ideological factors that led to their radicalisation, such as the sense of belonging and identity, critical thinking skills to discern radical rhetoric online, mental resilience, correlated stresses; and in particular, efforts are made to enable detainees to continue with their education where it is practicable.

sections.label: NCCS Christian counsellor for youth
sections.summary: ISD is working closely with the National Council of Churches of Singapore to identify a suitable Christian counsellor for the youth's rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: In addition, ISD is working very closely with the National Council of Churches of Singapore, NCCS, which is keen to be involved in the youth's rehabilitation to identify a suitable Christian counsellor for him.

sections.label: ISD engagement with religious groups
sections.summary: ISD regularly engages religious groups, sharing the current situation and signs to look out for, including propensity for violence and attitudes towards multiculturalism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Yes, Sir, ISD regularly engages the religious groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: And in the engagements, besides sharing with them what is the current situation, one of the things that we always share with them is to look out for the signs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: I have highlighted during my speech earlier on the signs that we have to look out for – one, the propensity for violence, a misguided understanding of certain religious beliefs and, of course, some signs about the individual's attitude towards multiculturalism and multiracialism.
